messages:
aj: Heads up — seeing an eviction wave in eu-west1 around 08:12 UTC. GPU pods reporting 'NetworkUnavailable' then preempted. Suspect ENI egress limits hitting racks with heavy model download traffic.

maria: I noticed autoscaler spikes + backfill at the same time. Do you have node/pod events or logs? Any recent taint/affinity changes?

aj: pasted node events:
```
Type    Reason                 Age   From               Message
Warning NetworkUnavailable     2m    kubelet, ip-10-0  Network plugin failed to set up pod "...": failed to allocate ENI: resource exhausted
Normal  NodeNotReady           1m    kubelet           Node ip-10-0 marked NotReady
Warning Evicted               30s   kubelet           The node had condition: NetworkUnavailable, evicting pods
```
Also saw CNI errors in kubelet logs: "eni-alloc: rate limit exceeded, 429" and a few TCP retransmits in dmesg.

kevin: Sharing grafana -> ENI tx errors jump at 08:10, NAT gateway QPS near soft limit, and az3 shows highest queueing. Pod restart counts + descheduler runs line up. Could be egress hotspoting from model downloads + logging burst.

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0423-eni-throttle-eu-west1. Paging oncall @oncall-eng.

jules: If kubelet marks Node NotReady because of CNI, the scheduler/descheduler will preempt GPU pods due to the NoExecute taint (node.kubernetes.io/not-ready). We should avoid immediate eviction on transient network blips — we saw similar oscillation last quarter.

ops-jen: Mitigation options: 1) bump node-level drain-delay so we don't evict for short NetworkUnavailable windows (10m). 2) Mark critical GPU workloads with a longer toleration or a custom disruption policy. 3) Move egress-heavy infra (model caches / artifact pulls) to dedicated egress ENI pools. Downside: delays recovery for truly unhealthy nodes.

maria: Can we make the scheduler treat 'NetworkUnavailable' differently from kernel/network-failure? E.g., add a predicate to avoid evicting pods on nodes with only ENI allocation failures. Also consider increasing NAT throughput or adding ephemeral ENI pool.

kevin: Short-term playbook: patch descheduler to increase scheduling.delaySeconds and disable aggressive backfill for GPU job label (redwood/gpu=true). Also add a temporary rule to keep pods with label redwood/critical=true pinned. Long-term: adjust ENI autoscaler to pre-warm ENIs on racks running large-model downloads.

aj: I'll open a runbook PR now with the descheduler tweak + list of kubectl commands. Attaching a piped log excerpt for the affected pod:
```
2026-04-23T08:11:21Z kubelet: Pod "trainer-xyz" failed to create network: eni-alloc: rate limit exceeded
2026-04-23T08:11:28Z kubelet: marking node NotReady due to CNI
2026-04-23T08:12:01Z kubelet: Evicting pod "trainer-xyz" due to node condition
```
I'll also create the incident timeline and tag networking.

maria: Great — flag me on the PR. We should also run a smoke test after the change to ensure no regression in node recovery.

aj: Will do. If we need urgent capacity, ops-jen can spin up a warm ENI pool in az3.

ops-jen: On it, starting warm ENI reserve. Will report back when ready. :white_check_mark:
